verdicts.evidence: Carried from round 1 (was c001); claim text unchanged. Reuters: French officials 'on Monday accused Iran's Revolutionary Guards of responsibility' for the October attacks. NPR: ANSSI said Iranian military hackers 'took over refrigeration controllers at around 700 different retail sites in France'. Barrot confirmed IRGC responsibility (The Record). Tag ALLEGED is right.
Carried from round 1 (was c002); claim text unchanged. NPR: on Tuesday Iran's Foreign Ministry rejected 'baseless and malicious allegations'.

Round 2, re-read. Help Net Security, Nov. 9: 'Pro-Russian groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest claimed the supermarket attacks on November 4', 'but investigators haven't confirmed the claim'. Cybernews: the two 'have claimed shared responsibility'; 'the allegations cannot be independently verified'; researcher CyberKnow doubts they breached anything. Anadolu, Nov. 4: claim seen by Rai, about Monday's incidents (Nov. 2). TechTimes: they claimed the November wave. The page's sentence matches Help Net Security almost word for word and sits after the sentence on the November wave, so it reads correctly here. The preceding sentence ('No government has attributed ...') holds: The Record says the ANSSI report does not address November. WATCH is acceptable for an unverified claim. Every outlet that gives a scope ties the claim to the November wave; saying so would be tighter.
verdicts.fix: Optional, not blocking: 'have claimed the November supermarket attacks'.

verdicts.evidence: Carried from round 1 (was c004); claim text unchanged. Advisory 'US Government Partners Urge Hardening Industrial Refrigeration and Cold Chain Monitoring Systems', 'As of November 5, 2026', authored by CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DoT.

Round 2, re-read. Now attributed to the minister alone. AP and ITV: Lescure told Parliament on Tuesday Oct. 13 'about 700 of the country's 10,000 supermarkets were affected'. Night of Oct. 11-12 per IT-Connect and TechTimes.

Carried from round 1 (was c006); claim text unchanged. Reuters: fridges and freezers 'as high as 50 degrees Celsius' for about six hours at Intermarche stores, 'sparking fires'. AP: '50 degrees Celsius (122 degrees Fahrenheit)' per BFM-TV. The Record: at least 15 fires. Note: the six-hour duration rests on Reuters/Intermarche alone; 'at some stores' keeps it in bounds.
Carried from round 1 (was c007); claim text unchanged. The Hacker News: 'Danfoss declared the AK-SM 800 end-of-life in May 2021 and phased out the AK-SC 355 in 2016.'

Carried from round 1 (was c008); claim text unchanged. Nextgov, Oct. 28: 'Several steps still stand between the program and labeled products reaching store shelves'; 'The FCC must finish its technical requirements and testing procedures' before test labs are accredited. The article never says 'zero' in terms; it follows from no lab being accredited. No later report of a certified product found (search, Nov. 10).

Carried from round 1 (was c009); claim text unchanged. Labeled inference. EFS: 'monitoring and alarm systems quickly detected the temperature change' (BleepingComputer); an on-call technician spotted the rise (Le Quotidien du Medecin, IT-Connect). No patch is reported.

Carried from round 1 (was c010); claim text unchanged. Le Quotidien du Medecin, citing Le Canard enchaine: cold rooms 'ont ete programmees pour atteindre 110 C'. IT-Connect: 'Cela ne signifie pas que les poches de plasma ont atteint 110 C'. Newsweek: attackers 'changed the setting to 110 degrees'. Cited FrenchBreaches and U.S. Sun could not be opened; verified on other outlets.

Carried from round 1 (was c011); claim text unchanged. The Hacker News: AK-SM 800A units hit 'were running outdated firmware, according to Danfoss's statement'. Reuters: affected units 'were running outdated firmware'.

Carried from round 1 (was c012); claim text unchanged. The Record: Danfoss's October newsletter said it was enforcing a 'hard End of Service' policy for legacy products. The Hacker News dates the newsletter to October 2025.

Carried from round 1 (was c013); claim text unchanged. The Record, Nov. 2: Danfoss and Copeland both said the affected devices were mainly discontinued products that no longer received security updates.
Carried from round 1 (was c014); claim text unchanged. The Record: Sabcobel knew of about 20 affected units, which 'needed physical modifications and not just a software update'.

Carried from round 1 (was c015); claim text unchanged. The Register, Oct. 13: 'more than 4,500 endpoints were exposed as of Monday, with more than half of those located in France'. Timing is loose: the count is as of Monday Oct. 12, the day after the attack, not 'days after'.

Carried from round 1 (was c016); claim text unchanged. Claroty: '2765 exposed devices according to Censys'; CVE-2025-41450, -41451, -41452; fixes in 4.2 (for -41450) and R4.3.1. CISA ICSA-25-140-03 (May 20, 2025) covers only CVE-2025-41450 and R4.2; the other two CVEs and R4.3.1 rest on Claroty and Danfoss.

Carried from round 1 (was c017); claim text unchanged. Hackread, Oct. 26: 12,976 exposed observations in 99 countries and territories (Forescout Vedere Labs); Danfoss StoreView 4,697 services. 'Services' is the right unit; they map to 6,017 IP addresses.

Carried from round 1 (was c018); claim text unchanged. The Register, Sept. 2, 2025: ten Frostbyte10 flaws found by Armis in Copeland E2 and E3; E2 end of life in October; Copeland's Josh Weaver: 'about two-thirds of grocery stores in North America use its products'.

Round 2, re-read. Reuters, Oct. 13: agency said 'the refrigeration systems of Copeland and Dixell were also hacked'; Copeland 'declined to confirm'. SecurityWeek, Oct. 15: CERT-FR added Copeland XWEB and Dixell XWEB; Copeland 'first declined to confirm the findings but later acknowledged a vulnerability'. Newsweek: 'Copeland confirmed a vulnerability in some discontinued controllers'. XWEB is a different line from the E2/E3 of Frostbyte10 (The Register, 2025).

Round 2, re-read. AFP via Boursorama: 80 of about 2,000 U stores; CEO: 'pas clients directs de Danfoss', 'Nous sommes clients d'acteurs frigoristes qui nous mettent a disposition cette solution'. The page now says this.

Carried from round 1 (was c021); claim text unchanged. Read the advisory itself: no U.S. incident reported; activity described as 'targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems globally'; refers only to 'malicious cyber actors'. Nextgov: 'The U.S. notice does not name who is responsible'.

Carried from round 1 (was c022); claim text unchanged. Open as of Nov. 10. The Register, Nov. 5: it knows of no documented attacks on refrigeration in U.S. supermarkets. Help Net Security, Nov. 9: no U.S. victims among named countries. Military commissaries are the only U.S. cases, and those are 'suspected'.
Carried from round 1 (was c023); claim text unchanged. Labeled inference describing the page's own scale.

Round 2, re-read. Labeled inference, now hedged to 'most' twice. Fits the facts: AK-SC 355 phased out 2016 and AK-SM 800 end of life 2021 are the bulk of what Danfoss says was hit; the rules in the table date from 2020 to 2027.

Carried from round 1 (was c025); claim text unchanged. Commission: from 11 September 2026 early warning within 24 hours, notification within 72 hours, final report 'no later than 14 days after a corrective measure is available'. Art. 13(8): 'the support period shall be at least five years' unless expected use is shorter. Main obligations from 11 December 2027 (Jones Day). See flag on the 'NO' cell beside it.

Carried from round 1 (was c026); claim text unchanged. SGS: from 1 August 2025 RED cybersecurity requirements (Art. 3.3 d/e/f) mandatory for 'all radio equipment placed on the market'; EN 18031-1/-2/-3 harmonized standards.
Carried from round 1 (was c027); claim text unchanged. heise: update guarantee of five years 'after the end of sales', in force June 20, 2025.

Carried from round 1 (was c028); claim text unchanged. UK: regime 'came into effect on 29 April 2024'; prohibits universal default passwords; requires published minimum security update period (gov.uk). WATCH half: gov.uk lists no enforcement action; searches on Nov. 10 turned up no OPSS penalty under PSTI. The claim is worded as 'found', which is as far as the record goes. The cited Modern Regulator page could not be opened.

Carried from round 1 (was c029); claim text unchanged. SB 327: 'a reasonable security feature or features'; a preprogrammed password 'unique to each device manufactured' qualifies; operative January 1, 2020; devices 'sold or offered for sale in California'.
Carried from round 1 (was c030); claim text unchanged. Nextgov: 'voluntary program'; FCC 'selected ioXt Alliance as lead administrator in April'.

Carried from round 1 (was c031); claim text unchanged. Same basis as c008: implied by Nextgov (testing requirements and lab accreditation still pending), not stated outright. REPORTED is the right ceiling.

Carried from round 1 (was c033); claim text unchanged. DOJ, April 7, 2026: 'court-authorized technical operation'; FBI sent commands to compromised TP-Link routers.

Carried from round 1 (was c034); claim text unchanged. The Register: CERT-FR 'advised disconnecting or restricting network access' and 'recommended a factory reset, security patches, credential rotation'. Alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 published Oct. 12 (The Hacker News).

Carried from round 1 (was c036); claim text unchanged. DTN: compliance reports to the FTC every 60 days, verified by the CEO. FTC release says only 'strict reporting and oversight requirements'.

Carried from round 1 (was c037); claim text unchanged. DTN: Deere must use 'reasonable best efforts' to get approval from a third party whose software is embedded; until then ECU capabilities are not required. Extensions on showing 'good cause'.

Carried from round 1 (was c038); claim text unchanged. Commission: 'As of 11 September 2026, manufacturers are required to report actively exploited vulnerabilities'; early warning within 24 hours; submitted through ENISA's Single Reporting Platform.

Round 2, re-read. The limit now separates the two duties. Art. 69(3): reporting obligations 'apply to all products with digital elements that were placed on the market before 11 December 2027, whether or not they are ever modified'; the Art. 13 design and support duties apply to products placed on the market from Dec. 11, 2027. The table cell now reads 'PARTLY Reporting yes; design and support duties no', which matches. Enforcement untested: no action found.
Carried from round 1 (was c040); claim text unchanged. heise: five years of updates 'after the end of sales'.
Carried from round 1 (was c041); claim text unchanged. heise: Google 7 years; Samsung 7 for flagships, 6 for A-series; Honor 7 for top models, 'at least 6' for others.

Carried from round 1 (was c042); claim text unchanged. heise: Motorola's lawyers say the regulation 'merely stipulates that updates must be made available free of charge', not 'a guaranteed obligation'.

Carried from round 1 (was c043); claim text unchanged. DOJ: GRU unit 26165 hijacked TP-Link routers; FBI reset DNS settings and blocked the GRU's original access; 'in more than 23 states' (FBI Boston SAC, in the release).

Carried from round 1 (was c044); claim text unchanged. DOJ: steps 'can be reversed by legitimate users at any time through factory resets'; no count of remediated U.S. routers, only 'thousands' compromised worldwide.
Carried from round 1 (was c045); claim text unchanged. Labeled inference. Facts beneath it hold: CERT-FR alert Oct. 12; Reuters: PM Lecornu 'instructed ... ANSSI to investigate'.

Carried from round 1 (was c046); claim text unchanged. Labeled inference. Facts beneath it hold: attribution, summons, warrants and sanctions push on Nov. 9-10, four weeks after Oct. 11-12 (Reuters, Al Jazeera, The Record). None imposes a duty on makers.
Carried from round 1 (was c047); claim text unchanged. Labeled inference; the table's supported rows bear it out.

Carried from round 1 (was c048); claim text unchanged. The Record: Danfoss enforcing 'hard End of Service' for legacy products; the affected devices were mainly discontinued products without security updates.

Round 2, re-read. ADT release (as filed with the SEC): '$10.00 per share in cash', '$15.3 billion in enterprise value', Oct. 29, 2026. OpenAI, Dec. 1, 2025: 'OpenAI takes an ownership stake in Thrive Holdings'. Both primary; FACT is right now that the Apple sentence has its own tag.

Round 2, re-read. Mostly right now, one detail too firm. 9to5Mac: Apple states customers 'will be able to pay an additional fee to have their Apple Home Collection accessories professionally installed by ADT through Apple Retail'; TidBITS: 'Apple Retail offers third-party installation from ADT for an additional charge'. The cameras are LG's. But no source says the cameras go on sale in December: TidBITS: 'available starting in December 2026' with 'select accessories arriving in early 2027'; Techlicious: 'Apple hasn't said which ones those are'. My round 1 suggested wording had this same flaw.
verdicts.fix: Apple says its retail arm will offer ADT installation, for a fee, for its Apple Home Collection, which includes LG-made cameras and starts going on sale in December 2026.

Round 2, re-read. Al Jazeera: investigation into Shahid Kaveh; 'requested international arrest warrants be issued for two Shahid Kaveh officials'. The Record: judicial investigation 'against the head of the Shahid Kaveh unit', two deputies and unidentified others; 'requested international arrest warrants for the suspects', no number. Carried from round 1 (was c066); claim text unchanged. NPR quotes Ari Ben Am (FDD) and Alex Orleans (Sublime Security): the group 'is repeating a pattern here'. They say it fits the unit's record; neither verified it. 'Plausible' does not exceed that.
Carried from round 1 (was c067); claim text unchanged. NPR: Iran's Foreign Ministry rejected 'baseless and malicious allegations'.

Round 2, re-read. The whole bullet, not only its last sentence. Two parts hold: the report is public and five pages (The Record: 'five-page report', CERTFR-2026-CTI-009); no other government has joined (NPR: Rubio declined; TechTimes: Kallas, 'no specific EU measures'). One part goes past its source: 'is reported to list no technical indicators'. TechTimes says only that 'Its web page for report CERTFR-2026-CTI-009 lists no indicators of compromise and names no vulnerability' and that it 'links a full PDF report'; it does not say what the PDF contains. The Record says the report describes 'Farsi text artefacts, tooling, and reconnaissance infrastructure' and has an annex naming people. I could not open the report (fetch refused both cert.cyber.gouv.fr and cert.ssi.gouv.fr). Also still unmentioned: TechTimes, citing Reuters via Tribune, says 'Microsoft privately linked Iran to the October sabotage at least two weeks before the French announcement' and declined comment; not public confirmation, but relevant to 'no independent confirmation'.
verdicts.fix: France's attribution report is public (CERTFR-2026-CTI-009, five pages); its web page is reported to list no indicators of compromise. This brief relies on press accounts of it. We found no public independent confirmation and no other government joining the attribution.

verdicts.evidence: Carried from round 1 (was c069); claim text unchanged. Labeled inference; a standard caution, not contradicted by any source read.

Round 2, re-read. The Record: the ANSSI report does not address the November wave; no outlet reports an attribution of the blood service incident; commissary cases rest on anonymous suspicion ('the Pentagon has not made any official statement', NPR). Worded as 'no government has attributed', which is what the record shows. Still open today.

Round 2, re-read. New bullet; read whole: 'There is a competing account. Pro-Russian groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest have claimed the supermarket attacks; investigators have not confirmed those claims.' The claim is real and REPORTED is right. Help Net Security, Nov. 9: 'Pro-Russian groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest claimed the supermarket attacks on November 4', 'but investigators haven't confirmed the claim'. Cybernews: the two 'have claimed shared responsibility'; 'the allegations cannot be independently verified'; researcher CyberKnow doubts they breached anything. Anadolu, Nov. 4: claim seen by Rai, about Monday's incidents (Nov. 2). TechTimes: they claimed the November wave. What the sources do not support is 'competing account' in a block about who did the October attack in France. Every outlet that states a scope puts the claim on the November wave, which France has not attributed to anyone; none says the groups claimed Oct. 11-12. SentinelOne adds that Z-Pentest's own post concerns 'a Spanish supermarket' and 'confirms neither access nor damage, nor any link to the current attacks'. My round 1 note called this 'the main competing account'; on a closer read that was too strong.
verdicts.fix: Separately, pro-Russian groups NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest have claimed the November wave of supermarket attacks; investigators have not confirmed those claims, and one researcher doubts the groups did more than claim credit. No source reports that they claimed the October attack.

verdicts.evidence: Carried from round 1 (was c071); claim text unchanged. Labeled inference tying to an in-development piece.

Round 2, re-read. The whole checkpoint: 'Whether France publishes technical indicators beyond its five-page attribution report or a court tests the case, and whether any government attributes the November wave. Whether the October and November waves are linked.' The last two questions are open (Reuters could not establish a link; no attribution of November). The first presumes the report holds no technical indicators. I cannot tell: TechTimes says only the web page lists none and that a full PDF is linked; The Record does not say. Tried cert.cyber.gouv.fr/cti/CERTFR-2026-CTI-009/ and the cert.ssi.gouv.fr equivalent; the fetch tool refused both, and a search did not surface the document.
verdicts.fix: Safe wording until someone reads the PDF: 'Whether France publishes evidence outsiders can test, or a court tests the case, ...'
